extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, political reformers, and students of political theory (early-20th-century American context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative criteria for reconstructing American state and municipal political institutions within a federal system, emphasizing responsibility, efficiency, and the relation between national and democratic principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical justification for colonial expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: The validity of colonial expansion for a democracy is a 'manifest deduction' only if the people whose independence is diminished are incapable of efficient national organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonial rule must rest on a demonstrated incapacity of the colonized to self-organize; additionally, a democratic colonizer has an unusually high obligation to provide for the economic prosperity, educational discipline, and social improvement of colonial populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: National-interest test for colonies
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of territory should be evaluated by national interest — weighing responsibilities and costs against benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote colonies may be more of a responsibility than a source of national power; consider financial cost, loss of life, defense difficulties, and whether possession advances essential national interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic value relative to wider foreign policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of a colony must be judged in relation to broader strategic concerns (e.g., influence in a theatre such as the Far East).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if militarily costly (e.g., Philippines requiring a Pacific fleet), possession may have political advantages by keeping public opinion engaged with regional problems such as China and Japan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonies as instruments for public awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of overseas territories can help shape domestic public opinion toward engagement with complex foreign problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peculiar value of certain colonies may be less direct material benefit than their role in making the public realize the scale and cost of projecting power and protecting interests abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic responsibility to international peace (preparedness to use force)
rubrics_metrics.description: A peace-preferring democratic nation must be 'spiritually and physically prepared to fight for' peace; neutrality may be irresponsible under some conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peace will prevail because of the 'righteous use of superior force'; therefore foreign policy should not equate a preference for peace with refusal to intervene when necessary to secure a pacific order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active contribution to a pacific system of public law
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States should be prepared to interfere under certain circumstances in European or global complications to help establish a pacific international order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects an absolutist isolationism rooted in a romanticized Monroe Doctrine; Americanism should not be indifferent or suspicious of the spread of democracy in Europe, and Pan-Americanism should be grounded in democratic purpose rather than mere geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility of national policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A national policy must be flexible without being invertebrate and must apply concretely to diverse specific problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should be adaptable to radically different problems while retaining core principles; it should counsel patience but oppose collective indifference or irresponsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature radical reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pursue radical reforms until American public opinion is converted to a fuller realization of national responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical proposals should be moderate and linked to a persistent challenge to popular prejudices; timing and public readiness are crucial for durable reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus reforms on state and municipal institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: State and municipal political machinery are the natural and useful subjects for reconstructive experiments rather than fundamental amendments to the Federal Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary state constitutions are ephemeral and local forms are often more changeable; immediate efforts should target the most palpable weaknesses in local administration and government.

rubrics_metrics.name: State governments must effectively perform core functions
rubrics_metrics.description: State governments should competently preserve order, administer civil and criminal justice, collect taxes for general and local purposes, and be responsible for public education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of state governments should examine their record on law-and-order, effectiveness of criminal courts, civil justice integrity, tax collection fairness and productivity, and the adequacy of educational systems for an industrial democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal justice effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal laws and judicial processes must function to punish malefactors appropriately and deter lawlessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticizes laws 'framed... for the benefit of the lawyers and their clients' and notes that dubious judicial methods contribute to lynching and disorder; reform should reduce dilatory processes and ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial independence and insulation from party machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges should not be demoralized by short elective terms or be 'creatures of the political machine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short terms and elective dependence encourage patronage and subservience; judiciary reforms should increase independence, longer tenure or appointment mechanisms to improve beneficent influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-system reform
rubrics_metrics.description: State tax systems based on the old property tax are unjust and unproductive and must be transformed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State legislatures have been unable to reform tax bases; a reformed, just, and productive taxation scheme is required as part of state-level reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education adapted to industrial democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Public education must be intelligent and well-informed, adapted to the needs of an industrial and agricultural democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although generally liberal, state educational systems are chaotic and imperfectly adapted; reforms should aim for systems that meet contemporary economic and social needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative wisdom and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: State legislatures should enact coherent, non-ephemeral, and honest legislation that increases respect for representative government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques current state legislatures for trivial, contradictory, corrupt laws, occasional repudiation of debts, and vacillation between confiscation and favoritism toward corporations; legislative reform must improve competence and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize state institutions to match restricted federal-era functions
rubrics_metrics.description: State political institutions should be adapted to their necessarily restricted functions within a Federal system rather than modeled as smaller copies of national government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because states surrendered major functions to the Federal government, their organizational design should reflect narrower responsibilities; failure to adapt produced mal‑adaptation and inefficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate responsibility to ensure accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: A reconstructive aim should be to concentrate responsibility and power so that mistakes and abuses have unmistakable and absolute responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentration can be achieved either by subordinating the legislature to the executive or vice versa; the goal is clear accountability so reformers controlling government can enact effective change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassess the system of checks and balances at state level
rubrics_metrics.description: The triple division of powers (checks and balances) may be disadvantageous in state governments where concentrated efficiency is more important than maximal safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While checks and balances protect against despotism at the national level, at state level they can divide responsibility and hinder cooperation; consider alternative structures that promote effective local governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful use of initiative and referendum
rubrics_metrics.description: The initiative and referendum transfer legislative authority directly to the people and substitute direct government for representative government; such a substitution should be justified by comprehensive analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although initiated to remedy legislative betrayal, direct legislation abandons the tradition of representation and should not be adopted unless it demonstrably remedies the causes of legislative failure without unacceptable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design representative bodies to have meaningful responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If the public wants better legislatures, it must give them something substantial to do or arrange for them to perform a limited but definite service capably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State constitutions have hedged legislatures into trivial roles; either expand their substantive responsibilities or redesign them so that they can competently fulfill a well-defined function, thereby improving the quality of representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address root organizational causes of corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: When many representatives exercise authority improperly, the problem often lies in the system of organization as much as in individual turpitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms should focus on altering the system that 'has been organized for the benefit of corrupt and inefficient men'—structural change rather than sole reliance on moralizing about individuals.
